The Console surfaces a top-down view and lets you drill into specific routes. (screen share) Sorry if the slide is fuzzy — screen resolution on my end is low.

[00:01:07] Leah: For example, support-chat (your busiest route) typically has short prompts but lots of sessions, doc-qa has high token variance due to long contexts.

[00:01:28] Leah: Good point — Console shows both rows: raw tokens and billing tokens after model-specific tokenization. We also provide an export that maps requests to invoice line items — so your finance team can ingest it into your chargeback system.
[00:01:40] Mark: So that export will give us request id -> billed tokens -> route -> model?
[00:01:44] Leah: Exactly, plus timestamp and model variant. We also include cost-per-token at the time of the request so you can do exact per-request cost.

[00:01:51] Ari: On the billing side we talked about routes mapped to cost centers. You can tag a route with owner, product, and cost-center ID. That drives the chargeback CSV.
[00:02:01] Nina: Nice. I want to see examples mapped to our chart of accounts.
[00:02:04] Ari: We'll attach a sample CSV that maps to auriga-sample-workload.csv — it's in the shared folder.

[00:02:12] [00:02:12] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[00:02:15] Leah: Another feature — live cost simulation. You can change model mix (e.g., switch doc-qa from base-7b to base-13b or to an fp16 quantized variant) and the Console recalculates expected spend for the window you select.
[00:02:29] Diego: Is that using historical latency/throughput or sample-based estimate?
[00:02:32] Leah: It's hybrid — we use your historical token distribution plus our performance profiles for the model/hardware combos. If you want, we can re-run a microbenchmark with your real prompts to tighten the estimate.
[00:02:43] Mark: That microbenchmark is one of the things we want. We need to quantify latency SLO impact when moving to a cheaper quantized model.
[00:02:51] Ari: Perfect lead into the pilot. We recommend a three-route pilot: 1) support-chat, 2) doc-qa, 3) billing-assist. That gives coverage for low-token-high-qps, high-token-variable, and sensitive-financial calls.

[00:03:18] Diego: I need to flag that our compliance team needs to see the audit trail for keys and model version rollouts.
[00:03:24] Leah: We have detailed audit logs — who changed a route, model pinning, rollout decisions. Logs are exportable and we support forwarding to your SIEM or to S3 for retention.
[00:03:34] Mark: What about SSO? We use Okta and SAML.
[00:03:37] Ari: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC roles for viewer/editor/admin, and can integrate with your IdP.
[00:03:44] Nina: KMS? We need customer-managed keys for any sensitive data.
[00:03:47] Leah: For Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with bring-your-key on dedicated plans. We'll share the KMS integration guide after the call.

[00:03:58] [00:03:58] Speaker 2: Yeahuh
[00:04:01] Ari: Let's return to the Console UI. I'm going to demo mapping traffic to cost-center tags. (screen share)
[00:04:09] Leah: See this route table — each row shows route name, owner tag, model variant, avg tokens, p95 latency, and hourly cost. You can filter by owner or by model.
[00:04:21] Diego: Can we group routes? We have multiple microservice endpoints that we want to roll up to a single product slug.
[00:04:25] Leah: Yes, there is a roll-up rule engine. You can create a grouping rule that matches route patterns (regex) and maps to a roll-up label. That roll-up will show aggregated tokens and cost.
[00:04:34] Mark: Nice, that will help with chargebacks.
[00:04:36] Nina: Another question — do you do anomaly alerts for sudden token spikes? We had a billing surprise last quarter.
[00:04:41] Leah: Anomaly detection exists. We have threshold alerts, and adaptive baselines. You can set alerts to go to Slack, email, or webhook. We also provide an automatic guardrail that can throttle a route if costs exceed a monthly burn threshold.
[00:04:55] Diego: Throttle — is that automatic or manual? We can't have an external outage.
[00:04:58] Leah: It's policy based and you can choose action: notify-only, soft-throttle (queue requests), hard-throttle (reject). Soft-throttle is often a safe starting point.

[00:05:06] Ari: Switching to model selection. For Auriga we recommend base-13b quantized for doc-qa in batch, and base-7b for support-chat with smaller kv caches to reduce latency.
[00:05:16] Diego: When you say kv cache, do you mean token-level KV caching across tokens in sessions?
[00:05:19] Leah: Yes KV cache for reused context, and prefix caching for common opening prompts. Those can reduce per-request compute by up to 30% depending on reuse.
[00:05:27] Mark: Any limits on prefix caching for privacy?
[00:05:29] Leah: You control retention windows and what is persisted. For Private deployments you can disable server-side persistent cache.

[00:05:35] [00:05:35] Speaker 3: okok
[00:05:36] Nina: Regarding cost modeling, how do reserved capacity discounts show up?
[00:05:41] Ari: The Console sim includes reserved capacity toggles: you can set a commit level and the model mix, and it will show expected unit cost and projected monthly savings vs pay-as-you-go. We can model burst capacity with a nominal surcharge.
[00:05:55] Diego: If we go Dedicated, what does the onboarding look like? We have to run in our VPC.
[00:06:00] Leah: Dedicated has a private compute pool; we provide a control plane integration. There's an onboarding checklist: network peering, route pinning, KMS, and initial model upload/pinning. On average onboarding takes 2–3 weeks for Dedicated deployments.

[00:06:18] Ari: We can do that.

[00:07:40] Leah: We support canary rollouts with traffic splitting, automatic rollback based on error/latency thresholds, and you can tie rollouts to eval suites so you can watch quality metrics as you increment traffic.
[00:07:51] Mark: Can we pin model versions per route for compliance?
[00:07:53] Ari: Yes model pinning is first-class. You can pin a SHA or a version label; the audit trail shows who pinned and when.

[00:07:59] [00:07:59] Ari: Okay shifting to the Optimize tab — this is where we show quantization recommendations and expected unit-cost delta.
[00:08:07] Leah: For your doc-qa workload, Optimize suggests fp16 quant with per-layer re-scale for low memory pressure. It also suggests a caching layer and increasing batch window for low-latency tolerant routes.
[00:08:20] Diego: Will that increase p95? We're very sensitive for support-chat.
[00:08:23] Leah: That's why Optimize attaches an estimated p95 delta per suggestion; for support-chat it suggests smaller batch windows and lower-latency model variants.
